items.informal_name: Commutativity of Partial Derivatives with Evaluation in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} [inst : CommSemiring R] {S : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommRing S]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] (p : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ τ) R) (f : τ → S) (j : σ),
  (MvPolynomial.aeval (Sum.elim MvPolynomial.X (⇑MvPolynomial.C ∘ f))) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl j)) p) =
    (MvPolynomial.pderiv j) ((MvPolynomial.aeval (Sum.elim MvPolynomial.X (⇑MvPolynomial.C ∘ f))) p)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ p $ in variables $ \sigma \oplus \tau $ with coefficients in a commutative ring $ R $, and an $ R $-algebra homomorphism evaluating variables in $ \tau $ via a function $ f : \tau \to S $, the partial derivative of $ p $ with respect to $ j \in \sigma $ commutes with evaluation. Specifically, evaluating the partial derivative $ \partial_{\text{inl}(j)} p $ using the homomorphism that maps $ \sigma $-variables to themselves and $ \tau $-variables via $ f $ is equivalent to first evaluating $ p $ under this homomorphism and then taking the partial derivative with respect to $ j $. This establishes $ \text{aeval}(\partial_{\text{inl}(j)} p) = \partial_j(\text{aeval}(p)) $ in the target algebra $ S $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative of Monomial with Respect to Variable i Follows Power Rule
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} {a : R} [inst : CommSemiring R] {i : σ} {n : ℕ},
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) ((MvPolynomial.monomial (Finsupp.single i n)) a) =
    (MvPolynomial.monomial (Finsupp.single i (n - 1))) (a * ↑n)
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, variable $ i \in \sigma $, natural number $ n $, and coefficient $ a \in R $, the partial derivative of the monomial $ a \cdot X_i^n $ with respect to $ X_i $ is $ a \cdot n \cdot X_i^{n-1} $. This follows the standard power rule for differentiation in multivariate polynomial rings.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Monomial in Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k n : ℕ) (r : R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = (Polynomial.monomial (n - k)) (↑(n.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the monomial $ rX^n $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ is given by $ \binom{n}{k} r X^{n - k} $. This expresses how the Hasse derivative acts on monomials by scaling the coefficient by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.

items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Derivation Induced by Function Acts as Function on Variables
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid A] [inst_2 : Module R A]
  [inst_3 : Module (MvPolynomial σ R) A] (f : σ → A) (i : σ), (MvPolynomial.mkDerivationₗ R f) (MvPolynomial.X i) = f i
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to A $ and any variable $ i \in \sigma $, the derivation induced by $ f $ satisfies $ D(X_i) = f(i) $.

items.informal_name: Derivation on Polynomial Variable Equals Function Value
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} (R : Type u_2) {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid A] [inst_2 : Module R A]
  [inst_3 : Module (MvPolynomial σ R) A] [inst_4 : IsScalarTower R (MvPolynomial σ R) A] (f : σ → A) (i : σ),
  (MvPolynomial.mkDerivation R f) (MvPolynomial.X i) = f i
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, $ R $-module $ A $, and function $ f : \sigma \to A $, the derivation $ D_f $ on the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ satisfies $ D_f(X_i) = f(i) $ for each variable $ X_i $, where $ X_i $ denotes the polynomial variable corresponding to index $ i : \sigma $.
